event_overview.title: About Democrats Prepare for Leadership Transition Amid GOP Impeachment Block
event_overview.subject: Democrats Prepare for Leadership Transition Amid GOP Impeachment Block
event_overview.summary: This event concerns a late-119th Congress dispute over an impeachment resolution targeting Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, alongside preparations for House leadership and organizational changes after the 2026 elections. On November 10, 2026, the House approved a motion to refer the resolution rather than advance it directly as an impeachment measure. The issue sits within the Constitution’s separate House-and-Senate roles in impeachment and the scheduled start of a new Congress in January 2027.

facts.label: House action
facts.value: On November 10, 2026, the House voted 211-204 to approve a motion to refer H. Res. 1655, titled “Impeaching Peter Brian Hegseth, Secretary of Defense, for high crimes and misdemeanors.”

facts.label: Allegations in the resolution
facts.value: The resolution’s articles alleged, among other things, that Hegseth acted in connection with military hostilities without the congressional authorization or conditions described in the War Powers Resolution; these were allegations in an impeachment proposal, not findings of guilt.

facts.label: Constitutional process
facts.value: The House has the sole power to impeach, while the Senate has the sole power to try impeachments; conviction requires the concurrence of two-thirds of senators present.

facts.label: Potential consequences
facts.value: Impeachment by the House alone does not remove an official. Following a Senate trial, the constitutional judgment available upon conviction is removal and possible disqualification from future federal office; ordinary criminal liability remains separate.

facts.label: Leadership transition timetable
facts.value: Terms of representatives and senators elected in 2026 begin at noon on January 3, 2027. House leadership is elected at the beginning of a new Congress, with the Speaker chosen by the full House.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the immediate House impeachment procedural dispute and the associated transition in congressional leadership, not the full history of U.S. military operations, all allegations against Hegseth, or every result of the 2026 elections.
